name: Directed Distance Field (DDF) for Gaussian Splatting
definition: A neural field that maps a ray (origin x and direction d) to the distance t to the first surface along d and a visibility value ξ (probability the ray hits). It serves as a constant-time, constant-memory ray oracle for secondary rays (shadows, AO, GI) in Gaussian Splatting scenes.
summary: Directed Distance Field is a neural implicit representation that provides constant-time, constant-memory ray queries for 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes using a small neural network.
